name: MVP pipeline: culture -> encapsulation -> load, lysis, wash -> barcoding -> sublibrary PCR -> release and cleanup
description: The current modules, in process order. Module 1 (MJ, final) grows the three cell types and delivers one counted suspension through p_mid; Module 2 encapsulates it (a parametric draft until MJ's redesign lands as chip/module2*.json, which the pipeline then picks up by itself); Module 3 (Szonja, translated into the chip-spec format) traps, lyses and washes the capsules; barcoding (split and pool, library steps 4-12) is not designed yet; Module 4 (MJ) splits into four sublibraries and runs index PCR; Module 5 (MJ) releases the DNA and cleans up the library. Older drafts (cad/m1_culture_spec.json, cad/m1b_cellprep_spec.json, cad/m3_wash_spec.json) are superseded and kept for reference only. TBC marks ports nobody has named yet; each hand-off's connector block says where the two modules' ports differ, i.e. where the dye demo needs an adapter.

modules.name: Module 1: culture (v1)

build.method: laser-cut acrylic: 3 mm base, 0.3 mm spacer (the cut layer), 3 mm lid
build.ports: 2 mm square holes through the 3 mm lid

modules.note: The chip for Sunday's food-dye demo (cad/module1_dye_demo.md). Design note: protocols/module1_design.md.

modules.name: Module 2: encapsulation

build.method: parametric draft (cad/generators/m2_encapsulation.py), PMMA layers; process to be set by the redesign

modules.note: Stand-in so the chain is complete. When a chip/module2*.json appears, tools/validate.py and the twin use it instead and warn if the hand-off ports below are not in it.

modules.name: Module 3: load, lysis, wash
modules.protocol_note: The steps (11) are in the source file's workflow block; not in protocol format yet.

build.method: TBC: the 25 um retention gap and 140 x 150 um channels are below laser-cut size

modules.note: Translated by tools/convert_module3.py; layout and valve construction are inferred (placeholder). Her file is the source of truth.

modules.name: Barcoding: split and pool (library steps 4-12)
modules.note: Module 3 hands its capsules to a split tree into well_01...well_16 described in barcoding_geometry.json, which is not in the repo yet.

modules.name: Module 4: sublibrary split + index PCR

build.method: hot-embossed COC (Tg >= 130 C), thermally bonded; 0.5 / 0.3 / 1.0 mm
build.ports: >= 0.8 mm drilled holes at >= 5 mm pitch, <= 6 per chip

modules.note: Filled one chamber at a time by an off-chip rotary valve (palindromic order), then thermocycled.

modules.name: Module 5: release + cleanup

build.method: hot-embossed COC (Tg >= 130 C), thermally bonded; 0.5 / 0.3 / 1.0 mm
build.ports: >= 0.8 mm drilled holes at >= 5 mm pitch, <= 6 per chip

modules.note: Collagenase release at 37 C, then magnetic bead capture; one sublibrary per pass.

to.note: The draft's core (cells) inlet; MJ's redesign may rename it.

connector.warning: Connector mismatch possible: Module 1 has 2 mm square lid holes; Module 2's ports are not decided. Expect an adapter from the square hole to tubing.

handoffs.note: One counted suspension leaves j_mid through p_mid (Module 1 protocol step 182).

from.note: The draft's capsule outlet; MJ's redesign may rename it.

connector.warning: Neither module's port style is decided; check before joining them with tubing.

handoffs.note: Cured capsules through Module 3's 100 um pre-filter into main_trap.

connector.warning: Barcoding is not designed; its inlet and port style are unknown.

handoffs.note: After step 11 of Module 3's workflow (back-flush resuspends the bed) into the split tree.

to.note: Through the off-chip rotary valve, one chamber at a time.

connector.warning: Module 4 takes 0.8 mm drilled ports at 5 mm pitch; barcoding's outlet is not designed. The rotary valve sits between them, so this is tubing either way.

from.note: Module 4 has no product outlet (in_s1-in_s4 and a shared vent); which port each sublibrary leaves through is not stated.

handoffs.note: One sublibrary per pass, by tubing between the chips (Module 5 protocol steps 1, 9, 17, 25).
Four libraries into tubes; pooling and size selection at the bench (Module 5 steps 33-34).
